Cc: security@medinex.com
Date: 2027-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request: signed region statement + connector evidence for EU pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the pilot. As part of our procurement/security intake I need two short things to close the legal review:

1) A signed region-boundary declaration confirming that Medinex tenant data for the pilot will be stored and processed in the EU (specific: eu-west-1) and that there will be no cross-border backups without explicit written request. A one-page PDF is fine.

2) Technical artifacts for PrivateLink/peering connectivity: a one-page network diagram of the connector (subnets, NAT/eip behavior), the list of egress IP ranges we should whitelist, and confirmation of whether KMS keys used for that deployment are customer-managed (BYOK) or Redwood-managed.

Also, if you have a prefilled SIG/CAIQ sheet for Medinex (we've started the SIG record), please attach that or point us to the file. We aim to have this packaged for the procurement team by EOD Wednesday (2027-04-13).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of InfoSec, Medinex Therapeutics
elena.soto@medinex.com

P.S. If some items need legal sign-off, a scanned signature is fine for now — we can follow up with DocuSign for the final SLA appendix.

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks for the request. We've prepared the artifacts and attached them here:
- redwood_region_boundary_v1.2.pdf (signed by Redwood Head of Legal) — confirms tenant data residency in eu-west-1, no backups to other regions unless requested in writing, and describes retention exceptions for snapshots required for platform recovery.
- privatelink_connector_map.png — simplified diagram showing PrivateLink endpoint in customer VPC, the connector subnet ranges, NAT behavior (connector NATs to a small egress pool owned by Redwood in same AZ), and suggested security groups and NACL snippets.
- sig_responses_medinex.xlsx — prefilled SIG/CAIQ responses with notes marking items that differ between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Key clarifications:
- KMS: For Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem package) we support BYOK — customer supplies KMS/HSM keys via a key import or by granting Redwood a CMK ARN for use. For Hosted API (standard tenant on Redwood multi-tenant), keys are Redwood-managed. For Dedicated (reserved capacity), we support both options depending on contract. For your EU PrivateLink pilot, BYOK is supported and we can include the KMS ARN field in the onboarding checklist.
- Egress IPs: The privatelink_connector_map includes the small egress CIDR ranges we use for outbound (we recommend allowing the 18.112.240.0/22 and 34.210.48.0/23 ranges for the connector; final list in the attachment).
- Audit logging & retention: Platform audit logs are retained 90 days by default in Hosted; for Private we can support 365 days per contract. We export audit events (tokenized) to a customer-owned S3 if requested.

Attachments are authoritative for this pilot; if you need signed annex language inserted into the MSA, let us know and legal will produce a one-paragraph addendum.

Markus Klein
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: redwood_region_boundary_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 1 page, signed), privatelink_connector_map.png (PNG, 1 diagram), sig_responses_medinex.xlsx (XLSX, 42 rows)
